declaration.preface: PennEngineering & Manufacturing Corp. (“PennEngineering”) (Group) is a global leader in engineered fastening solutions and installation technologies, serving industries including automotive, electronics, industrial machinery, and telecommunications. Through innovation, precision engineering, and high-quality manufacturing, PennEngineering delivers reliable products that enhance performance and support efficient assembly for customers worldwide.
declaration.declaration: PennEngineering is committed to responsible sourcing across its global supply chain, ensuring that procurement decisions promote ethical labor practices, respect human rights, maintain safe working conditions, and encourage environmentally responsible materials and processes. This Roadmap sets clear expectations for suppliers, contractors, and business partners to adopt sustainable, transparent, and ethical practices that align with the Company’s values and long-term commitment to supply chain sustainability.
declaration.scope: This Responsible Sourcing Roadmap to all PennEngineering operations, including manufacturing facilities, engineering centers, offices, and distribution activities globally. The roadmap applies to all employees, Workers, contractors, suppliers, and other stakeholders involved in the Company’s operations and value chain.

focusAreas: Conflict Minerals and Responsible Raw Material Sourcing
Conflict Minerals and Responsible Sourcing Performance Targets

Supplier Ethics Practices: Integrity and Ethical Conduct: PennEngineering promotes integrity, transparency, and ethical conduct across its supply chain. Suppliers are expected to conduct business in an ethical manner, avoid conflicts of interest, and comply with all applicable anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws and regulations.

Anti-Corruption and Anti-Bribery: Suppliers must prohibit all forms of bribery, corruption, fraud, and unethical business practices and must implement policies to ensure ethical conduct in all business transactions.
Conflict of Interest Management: Suppliers must disclose any actual or potential conflicts of interest and ensure that business decisions are made objectively and without improper influence.

Intellectual Property and Confidential Information Protection: Suppliers must protect confidential information, intellectual property, and sensitive business information shared by PennEngineering and its customers.
Supplier Social Practices: Workplace Health and Safety: PennEngineering expects suppliers to provide safe and healthy working conditions for all employees, implement appropriate occupational health and safety management practices, and take proactive measures to prevent workplace injuries and illnesses.

Human Rights and Labor Standards: PennEngineering is committed to protecting human rights across its supply chain. Suppliers are expected to prohibit child labor, forced labor, discrimination, and harassment, and to promote fair wages, reasonable working hours, and equal employment opportunities.
Fair Wages and Working Hours: Suppliers must comply with applicable wage laws, working hour regulations, overtime requirements, and legally mandated benefits.
Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion: Suppliers are encouraged to promote diversity, equity, and inclusion and provide equal opportunities for all employees.

Working Conditions and Employee Welfare: Suppliers should provide fair working conditions, including fair compensation, reasonable working hours, access to basic facilities, and a respectful workplace environment
Supplier Environmental Practices: Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Energy Management: Suppliers are encouraged to monitor and report greenhouse gas emissions, improve energy efficiency, and transition toward cleaner energy sources where feasible.
Water Management: Suppliers are expected to reduce water consumption, prevent water pollution, and comply with wastewater discharge regulations.
Pollution Prevention and Waste Management: Suppliers must reduce waste generation, control air and water emissions, and promote recycling and reuse of materials.

Materials, Chemicals, and Product Compliance: Suppliers must ensure compliance with environmental regulations and product requirements, including REACH, RoHS, and conflict minerals reporting requirements.
Product End-of-Life and Circular Economy: Suppliers are encouraged to consider product lifecycle impacts, including recyclability, reuse, and responsible disposal at the end of product life.
Environmental Management Systems: Suppliers are encouraged to implement environmental management systems such as ISO 14001 to improve environmental performance.
Conflict Minerals and Responsible Raw Ma: PennEngineering is committed to responsible sourcing of raw materials and supports efforts to eliminate the use of conflict minerals that directly or indirectly finance or benefit armed groups or contribute to human rights abuses. The Company conducts due diligence on the source and chain of custody of conflict minerals in accordance with internationally recognized due diligence frameworks and customer requirements.

PennEngineering requires relevant suppliers to provide conflict minerals information and declarations using recognized industry reporting tools such as the Conflict Minerals Reporting Template (CMRT) and Extended Minerals Reporting Template (EMRT). Suppliers are expected to provide information regarding the origin of tantalum, tin, tungsten, and gold (3TG), including smelter and refinery information, and to ensure responsible sourcing practices within their supply chains.

If conflict minerals sourced from high-risk regions are identified, suppliers are expected to implement corrective actions and transition to responsible or conflict-free sources. PennEngineering reserves the right to evaluate supplier compliance and may reconsider sourcing decisions if suppliers fail to meet responsible sourcing requirements.

PennEngineering is committed to complying with customer requirements and regulatory expectations related to conflict minerals and to supporting responsible mineral sourcing through supply chain transparency and due diligence practices
General Responsible Sourcing: PennEngineering establishes measurable targets to advance responsible and sustainable sourcing across its supply chain. These targets support continuous improvement in ethical business practices, workforce well-being, environmental stewardship, and supplier accountability.

targets.target: Ensure 100% of new suppliers complete ethics due diligence screening before onboarding each year.
Provide annual anti-corruption and ethical business conduct training to 100% of procurement employees by 2027.
Ensure 100% of suppliers sign confidentiality and intellectual property protection agreements by 2030.
Ensure 100% of suppliers implement whistleblower protection policies by 2030.
Ensure 90% of Tier 1 suppliers implement formal anti-corruption and ethics policies by 2030.
Maintain zero (0) cases of child labor, forced labor, or human trafficking across suppliers by 2030.
Ensure 100% of Tier 1 suppliers comply with working hours, wages, and labor law requirements by 2030.
Ensure 90% of Tier 1 suppliers implement formal human rights policies by 2030.
Increase supplier diversity participation (SMEs, minority-owned, or local suppliers) by 20% by 2030.
Ensure 100% of suppliers implement emergency preparedness and response procedures by 2030.
Ensure 100% of Tier 1 suppliers implement anti-discrimination and fair labor policies by 2030.
Ensure 100% of Tier 1 suppliers report Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions annually by 2030.
Ensure 80% of Tier 1 suppliers report Scope 3 emissions related to PennEngineering products by 2030.
Reduce supplier energy consumption by 20% by 2030 (from 2023 baseline).
Increase clean or renewable energy use to 30% at Tier 1 supplier facilities by 2030.
Reduce water consumption at supplier facilities by 15% by 2030.
Reduce supplier waste generation by 25% by 2030.
Ensure 70% of Tier 1 suppliers implement pollution prevention programs by 2030.
Ensure 50% of Tier 1 suppliers obtain ISO 14001 certification by 2030.
Ensure 100% of supplied materials comply with REACH and RoHS requirements each year.

policy.monitoring:
PennEngineering monitors the implementation of responsible sourcing practices through supplier ESG risk assessments, self-assessment questionnaires, supplier audits, performance evaluations, and sustainability data collection. Key performance indicators related to supplier environmental, social, and ethics performance are tracked and reviewed on a periodic basis.

The Procurement Department, in coordination with the Site Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) Team, is responsible for monitoring supplier compliance with the Supplier Code of Conduct, tracking supplier ESG performance indicators, reviewing assessment and audit results, and monitoring corrective action implementation. High-risk suppliers are subject to enhanced monitoring, including detailed assessments, audits, and corrective action follow-up.

PennEngineering maintains records of supplier assessments, audit findings, corrective action plans, supplier training, and supplier sustainability performance metrics. Responsible sourcing performance may be reported through internal management reviews, sustainability reports, customer sustainability assessments.
policy.reviewMechanism:
The Procurement Manager shall be responsible for conducting the annual review of this Responsible Sourcing Roadmap. The review will evaluate Roadmap effectiveness, supplier compliance with the Supplier Code of Conduct, progress toward responsible sourcing targets, supplier risk assessment results, and corrective action implementation status.

Any updates or revisions resulting from changes in regulatory requirements, customer requirements, supplier risk evaluations, audit findings, or operational changes will be incorporated into the roadmap and communicated to relevant internal stakeholders and suppliers.
